Sample for Pexels · 17 August 2026

Pexels media, in place

This page shows where your photographs and video segments appear inside our application, and what we did to them. The three panels below are the screens themselves: each was rebuilt from the application's own component code and its own design tokens, and each loads the exact files the application ships — nothing was re-exported or re-encoded for this page.

The application is a French offline meal planner, so the interface text is in French. Every caption on the right gives the English reading. Where a panel is interactive — opening a glossary term, playing a segment — it behaves as it does on a phone.

Today — one suggestion at a time

What the screen shows

One dish, proposed for the current meal. The photograph is the whole top of the card: full width, cropped to fill, no overlay and no text on top of it. Below it, the dish name, then the actions — Proposer autre chose (suggest something else), Voir la recette (see the recipe), J’ai choisi ce plat (I picked this one).

At the bottom, Dans le même esprit (in the same spirit) lists neighbouring dishes as small thumbnails.

The second thumbnail is not a broken image. 129 of the 330 recipes have a photograph. The rest fall back to a flat tint with the first letter of the dish, derived from the recipe’s own identifier — the same tint every time, on every device, with no network call. You are seeing the real fallback, not a placeholder we drew for this page.

It is also why we keep asking for photographs: 201 recipes out of 330 still show a letter.

Loading behaviour, as shipped

Main photo
eager. No loading="lazy" — it is the reason the screen exists.
Thumbnails
loading="lazy", decoded off the main thread.
Alt text
empty and aria-hidden: the dish name is already read out beside it, so a screen reader is not made to hear it twice.
Source
the file inside the application package. There is no remote URL anywhere in the markup.

How the photograph is placed

Position
first element of the page, before every control
Size
full width, 40% of the viewport height, never less than 12 rem
Fit
object-fit: cover — the frame is filled, the crop is centred
Corners
rounded to the card radius, unlike the suggestion card, which is flush
Overlay
none. No text, no gradient, no logo is drawn over it.
Fallback
the flat tint and initial, at exactly the same size — second panel on the left

What the recipe page is for

Ingredients scaled to the number of portions, the equipment, the numbered steps, and a single large action: Cuisiner pas à pas (cook step by step), which opens the step-by-step screen. The amber block at the bottom is a food-safety notice from the French food agency, carried by the recipe itself.

Underlined terms in the steps — Émincer, Tailler en dés — are glossary techniques. Tapping one opens its written definition in place, and nothing else: Émincer is one of the three techniques we filmed from your library, and its segment is not reachable from here. It lives on the glossary screen below, and only there.

Video

Cooking-technique glossary

3 techniques · 6 segments · all three sourced from Pexels

Gestes de cuisine

3 gestes

  • Couper un aliment en tranches ou en lamelles fines et régulières, à l’aide d’un couteau bien affûté, en général pour raccourcir un temps de cuisson ou obtenir une texture homogène.

  • Laisser un liquide s’évaporer à découvert pour le concentrer et l’épaissir. On réduit une sauce, jamais un aliment solide.

  • Verser un liquide (eau, jus, vin) dans une poêle ou une cocotte chaude après une cuisson, et gratter les sucs attachés au fond avec une spatule pour les dissoudre dans le liquide.

The glossary screen — click a term, then the frame

What the screen shows

A searchable list of cooking techniques. Every row carries the still frame of its first segment. Opening a row reveals the written definition, then the segment below it. When a technique has more than one moment, a strip lets the reader switch between them — Début (start), Milieu (middle), Fin (end). The segment always sits under the definition it illustrates; it is never reachable on its own.

Playback, exactly as shipped

Starts
only on a click. preload="none", so nothing is fetched until then.
Sound
muted, always. The source audio is not shipped.
Controls
none. No controls, and controlsList="nodownload".
Menu
right-click download and picture-in-picture are both disabled.
Loop
the 3 seconds repeat while the row stays open.

What each segment is

Duration
3.000 s, measured on every file above
Video frame
480 × 480 — a square crop of a landscape source
Poster frame
720 × 720 — one still, shown before playback and in the row above
Encoding
re-encoded twice, AV1 and H.264, plus that one JPEG still
Audio
none, stripped at import
Weight
115–217 kB per video file, 27–47 kB per poster

The source clips run far longer and are delivered at full resolution with sound. What ships is a three-second, silent, square, downscaled re-encode. The original cannot be reconstructed from it.

Files

The photographs themselves

129 shipped · 16 of them from Pexels

What each Pexels photograph is

Frame
1024 × 1024 — a square crop, on all 16
Encoding
AVIF, quality 45, well below the source
Weight
15–96 kB per file, 46 kB on average
Binding
one photograph, one recipe, by filename — there is no gallery

Across the whole catalogue the import caps the width at 1024 px and never enlarges; the crop is chosen per photograph, and for all sixteen Pexels files it came out square. The delivered originals are several megapixels and several hundred kilobytes; what ships is a downscaled, heavily recompressed derivative from which the original cannot be reconstructed.

Sixteen recipe photographs and all three techniques come from Pexels. The remaining assets are Creative Commons or public domain, credited in the same file and in the same form. The file is versioned with the source code, so a credit cannot be dropped without it showing in the history.

Constraints

What the application does not offer

By design, and testable

No route out of the app

  • No download, no export, no save for any photograph or segment.
  • No media browser, no gallery, no search over the media. A segment is reachable only through the technique it defines; a photograph only through its recipe.
  • The player exposes no native controls and no context menu.
  • Recipe sharing carries text only. The photograph does not travel with it.
  • Cook mode — the screen a user spends the longest on — shows no media at all.

Why the files must be embedded

  • The application runs entirely on the device. It has no server, no account, and no telemetry, and it must work with no connection at all.
  • That is a founding constraint of the project, not a preference. Streaming the media would break it.
  • The media ships inside the application package, alongside the catalogue, and is served from the device.
  • This page is built the same way: every photograph, segment, poster and typeface on it is embedded in the file you are reading. It works offline too.

Everything above is measured on the files the application ships, on 17 August 2026. The device panels are the application's own markup and its own design tokens; the media are the shipped files themselves, embedded in this page so it works without a network, as the application does.

If any part of this incorporation falls outside what the Pexels License permits, tell us which part and we will remove it.
